jobs.claim: Qiao et al. (2026) report that verifiers which see only fragmented slices of the reference can accelerate tail loss.

The channel the RLRF program claims reputation can resist is the one this study does not open, because its validators are stationary, its stake has no external value, and its weights are fixed before generation 1.

A validity filter judges whether an output is correct rather than whether it is rare, so where rare content is as checkable as common content such a filter can change rare composition only through the generator's own error profile, and if collapse proceeds by under-sampling rare modes no validity filter restores them, a reputation-weighted filter included.

A coin-flip family is a negative control, because a coin-flip pool knows nothing about validity, and if it meets the registered leak criterion or fails its acceptance rule, both substrates lose confirmatory status.

A threshold arm that accepts too few candidates fills the shortfall uniformly from rejected candidates, and an arm whose minimum over generations of the seed-mean fill-free share falls below 0.98 in a family has its tests there invalidated.
The pool under test omits most of what makes RLRF an institution: it has no economy, no strategy, no adversary, no deliberation, and no reputation dynamics after the single settlement.

A substrate was declared procedure-invalid by the operator before any run or reading, with no pre-run rule fired and no written reason recorded, and its nine registered tests stand at a p-value of one with no other label, so the filter is tested on one substrate, a two-dimensional mixture with simulated validators.

The preregistered pilot meant to confirm that every arm completes was never run, the confirmatory seeds ran without it, and the paper states that their later completion does not cure the skipped gate.

A positive reading on substrate G needs nine superior labels, and if the ten percent arm's retention exceeds 0.90 in a family the pool cannot be labeled superior to it there and no positive reading is possible.

The design names a failure pattern in advance: if the likelihood filter, the equal-weight pool, and the reputation pool each carry the negative label against full replacement in every family, the paper issues a registered sentence recording that each had lower capped retention at generation 50 than full replacement, as a registered negative result and not an implementation failure.

The two ways the oracle premise can fail license different readings: missing the registered margin is consistent with the validity-rarity limit without proving it, while failing the acceptance gate says nothing about whether perfect validity information helps, and either way no positive label can be attributed to validity filtering.

Because the simulated validators err independently given an accuracy that depends only on the tag, shared lineage, correlated errors, and error that depends on whether content is rare are excluded by construction, and the study supplies no evidence about correlated assessors or about reputation concentrating in a lineage.
Validity is balanced between rare and common content by construction, so the study says nothing about settings where rare content is harder to check.
Nine superior labels set a high bar, so a real but modest effect may be reported as not positive.

In the final audit rounds of the last three sections of the working draft, one audit family's command-line engines returned no verdict because their usage balance was exhausted, so those rounds hold two passing verdicts rather than three and left identified low-severity findings unadopted.
A replication of the published language-model protocol served as the gate for reading any outcome, and the published collapse result did not reproduce under the frozen rule.
Substrate G is not read, its outcomes stay sealed, substrate F is blocked as well, and the paper reports no filter result.
What domain scoping can govern is whose judgment of the domain-general validity bit counts, not what the bit says.

The design's pool supplies no reward signal and trains no policy, and its equal-weight contrast ablates the weights inside a data filter rather than inside policy training, so it does not supply the ablation the parent paper asks for.
The study runs no Full Vote, the staked and slashable second round of the parent protocol, and its single keyed update is not a stake settlement.
The pool seats five validators per candidate and nine when a candidate is contested, while the single verifier seats one.
The model engines that audited the study may share failure modes with each other and with the author's tools.
The study would not be in a position to say whether the implementation, those choices, or the published result accounts for the missed gate.
On this outcome the study examines nothing about the filter, and the narrow hypothesis remains unexamined.
The published protocol itself specifies twice as many epochs for the ten percent setting, and one confirming audit notes that the published study reported only minor degradation under that split.

One confirming audit finds that three choices can reverse the comparison between full replacement and the ten percent arm: retained real data was added to a full synthetic set while the public code keeps the original size and replaces the other rows with continuations, later generations were scored at their final epoch while generation 0 was scored at its best validation epoch, and the design fixed the learning rate schedule where the published methods left it open.
Neither the post-result review nor the audits established that those choices caused the miss, and the review licenses no claim about the filter and does not alter the Section VII reading.
Such a follow-on would still omit economic stake and deliberation, so it would test the parent mechanism only closer to its published form and not as a whole.
